what_its_for: Icosapent ethyl is a purified fish oil medicine used to lower very high triglyceride levels (a type of fat) in your blood. It is also used in adults who have heart disease or diabetes with other risk factors to lower the chance of having a heart attack, stroke, or other serious heart problems. It works alongside a healthy diet and other cholesterol-lowering medicines like statins.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with food. Do not break open, crush, dissolve, or chew the capsule. Taking it with a meal helps your body absorb the medicine better and may reduce stomach upset. Try to take it at the same times each day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual dose is 2 capsules (each 1 gram) taken twice a day with food, for a total of 4 grams per day. Always take the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once or extra doses to make up for one you missed.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the capsules in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect from heat and moisture. Keep out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it can raise your triglyceride levels and may make the medicine less effective. Tell your doctor if you take blood thinners like warfarin (Coumadin) because icosapent ethyl may increase your risk of bleeding. Be careful with any other fish oil or omega-3 supplements, as doubling up may not be safe unless directed by your doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: unusual bruising or bleeding that does not stop, signs of an irregular heartbeat such as a fast, pounding, or fluttering heartbeat or chest discomfort, swelling in your ankles or legs, or severe stomach pain. Also tell your doctor if you are allergic to fish or shellfish before starting this medicine.
when_it_works: You may start to see your triglyceride levels improve within a few weeks, but it can take several months to see the full benefit for your heart health. Keep taking this medicine even if you feel fine — it is working in the background to protect your heart. Continue following your low-fat diet and any exercise plan your doctor recommended.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Fish oil can pass into breast milk. Elderly patients: No special dose adjustment is usually needed, but let your doctor know about all other medicines you take. Fish or shellfish allergy: Tell your doctor right away, as this medicine is made from fish oil and may not be safe for you.
